new.title: Step inside Enschede's domed synagogue
new.desc: Designed by Karel de Bazel and opened in 1928, the synagogue on the Prinsestraat blends Amsterdam School and oriental touches under three copper domes, and is often called the most beautiful in the country.
new.tip: It is still a working synagogue, so join one of the guided openings run by the volunteer friends' foundation; the Volkspark is a two minute walk away.

new.title: Wander the textile workers' Volkspark
new.desc: Laid out in 1872 so mill workers had somewhere green to breathe, the Volkspark winds around a long pond dotted with monuments and artworks, right next to the city centre.
new.tip: Hunt for the monuments and artworks hidden along the paths, then loop back past the synagogue on the Prinsestraat.

new.title: Read the tiled walls of the Stadshaard in Roombeek
new.desc: Roombeek's heating plant is wrapped in Delft blue tiles that picture scenes from local history, a once mocked building that has become a quirky landmark of the rebuilt district.
new.tip: Walk around all sides before heading to the museums on Het Rozendaal; Roombeek was rebuilt after the 2000 fireworks disaster and every block has its own architect.

new.title: Get hands-on at De Museumfabriek
new.desc: The former TwentseWelle in Roombeek is now De Museumfabriek, a do-museum where Twente's textile past, natural history and inventions are meant to be touched and tried.
new.tip: Labels are mostly Dutch and German, so grab the app or a guide; the Rijksmuseum Twenthe is a short walk away for a double museum day.

new.title: See art meet technology at Tetem
new.desc: Tetem is Roombeek's art space for work that mixes modern art with technology, with bold exhibitions that rarely feel like a classic gallery.
new.tip: Combine it with a peek at the AKI ArtEZ art academy next door and its student work.

new.title: Cycle among the bunkers of old Vliegveld Twenthe
new.desc: North of the city, the military airfield that closed in 2016 has partly turned into a nature area where hangars, splitter boxes and bunkers hide among the trees.
new.tip: Follow the 25 km Fliegerhorstroute by bike and climb the lookout tower for a view over the former runways.

new.title: Walk the art route on the University of Twente campus
new.desc: The UT is the only Dutch university with a full campus, set in the woods of the old Drienerlo estate, with striking buildings like the Cubicus and the Bastille.
new.tip: Follow the campus Architecture and Art Route past the Zilverling, the Horst and the Bastille; the train stops at Enschede Kennispark next to the campus.

new.title: Sing along with FC Twente at De Grolsch Veste
new.desc: FC Twente plays its Eredivisie home games in the 30,000 seat stadium named after the Enschede brewed Grolsch, and the Tukkers in the stands are famously loud.
new.tip: Take the train to Enschede Kennispark, which stops right beside the stadium, and toast with a Grolsch from the club's home brewery city.

new.title: Cool off in the Rutbeek lake
new.desc: On the southwest edge of the city, the Rutbeek recreation area wraps a swimming lake in forest, with sandy beaches, water sports and even diving.
new.tip: Cycle out along the Rutbeek route; go early on hot days because the beaches fill up fast.

new.title: Graze the Twentsche Foodhal in the old Polaroid factory
new.desc: On the Performance Factory site, where looms and later instant film once ran, eight kitchens share one big hall and cook world food from local products.
new.tip: Kitchens only open later in the week and payment is card only; wander the skatepark and climbing gym on the same site afterwards.

new.title: Drink a New Enschede IPA at Stanislaus Brewskovitch
new.desc: What began in 2015 as a craft beer shop grew into a brew pub with its own brewery in a former church on the Stadsgravenstraat, plus a beer garden.
new.tip: Ask for the house brews first, then browse the shop shelves of specialty beers from small breweries to take home.

new.title: Take a terrace seat on the Oude Markt
new.desc: The heart of Enschede beats on this square of cafés around the Grote Kerk, a church whose oldest parts go back to around 1200.
new.tip: De Beiaard is a local favourite pub on the square; hop from café to café as the bells of the Grote Kerk ring.

new.title: Fry a slice of Twentse bakleverworst from the market
new.desc: This peppery liver and buckwheat sausage comes from the old home slaughtering days and is a Slow Food Ark of Taste product; Catholic Twente ate it after midnight mass on Christmas Eve.
new.tip: Buy it from a butcher's stall at the Van Heekplein market, slice it thick and fry it in butter on both sides, then eat it on rye bread.

new.title: Ride the steam tram line from Haaksbergen to Boekelo
new.desc: The volunteers of the Museum Buurtspoorweg run vintage steam trains over a 7.5 km local line through woods and over little steel bridges, past the old salt industry halt.
new.tip: Start at the 1884 station in Haaksbergen where you can watch the locomotives on the turntable; check the timetable since trains only run on set days.

new.title: Follow the wild bends of the Dinkel at the Lutterzand
new.desc: Between De Lutte and Denekamp the Dinkel still meanders freely, cutting steep sandy banks several metres high next to drift sands with heather and juniper.
new.tip: Park near the Kribbebrug on the Lutterzandweg and walk the marked loop along the river; it is open all year and lovely in autumn.

new.title: Hear farm stories at the Openluchtmuseum Ootmarsum
new.desc: The open-air museum gathers old Twente farmhouses, the Lös Hoes, and their tools to show how families lived on the traditional erven of the region.
new.tip: Afterwards stroll through Ootmarsum's protected old centre with its half-timbered houses and galleries.

new.title: Follow the midwinter horns through Ootmarsum
new.desc: From Advent to Epiphany, Twente blowers sound long wooden midwinterhoorns over the fields at dusk; in Ootmarsum you can walk a route past them at dusk.
new.tip: The evening walk starts at the VVV on the Markt on December Saturdays; reserve ahead and warm up at the fire with hot chocolate on the way.

new.title: Shop the summer Onion Market in Ootmarsum
new.desc: On a few Thursdays in late July and August the old streets of Ootmarsum fill with stalls and visitors for the Uienmarkt, the town's traditional summer market.
new.tip: Come early before the crowds and treat yourself to a slice of krentenwegge with coffee on the Markt.

new.title: Have coffee with krentenwegge in Ootmarsum
new.desc: The krentenwegge, a long loaf packed with currants and raisins, is Twente's most famous bake, and in Ootmarsum it comes thickly buttered with your coffee.
new.tip: Ask for a slice with butter at a café on the Markt; bakers sell whole weggen or a few slices to take home.

new.title: See Ruisdael's watermill at Singraven near Denekamp
new.desc: The Singraven estate on the Dinkel has a watermill with three wheels from 1448 that Jacob van Ruisdael painted; the canvas hangs in the National Gallery in London.
new.tip: Follow the Singraven signs from Denekamp and park at the mill; walk the estate avenues and arboretum, then have a drink at restaurant De Watermolen.

new.title: Browse the cabinets of Natura Docet in Denekamp
new.desc: Founded in 1911 by a local teacher, Natura Docet ('nature teaches') claims to be the oldest natural history museum of its kind in the country, full of minerals, fossils and mounted animals.
new.tip: Leave time for the landscape garden behind the museum, planted with species native to Twente.

new.title: Watch Judas sell the Easter pole in Denekamp
new.desc: On Easter Sunday Denekamp drags a tall spruce, the paasstaak, from the Singraven estate to the Easter meadow, hangs a tar barrel on top and lets 'Judas' sell it before the Easter fire is lit.
new.tip: Join the crowd following the tree through the village in the afternoon, then stay for the fire in the evening.

new.title: Climb the Tankenberg, the roof of Overijssel
new.desc: At 85 m the Tankenberg near Oldenzaal is the highest point of the province, crowned by a small domed tea pavilion known locally as the koepeltje.
new.tip: Cyclists tackle the steep Siemertweg from the Denekamp side; walkers can combine it with the nearby Paasberg in the Hooge Lutte woods.

new.title: Sit near Huttenkloas's chair at the Palthehuis in Oldenzaal
new.desc: This 17th century patrician house tells Oldenzaal's story from the Bronze Age to the textile era, with period rooms and the grim chair of the robber Huttenkloas, executed in 1775.
new.tip: The coach house holds a small centre on Oldenzaal's Hanseatic past with an interactive game; the basilica is around the corner.

new.title: Count salt shakers at the Zoutmuseum in Delden
new.desc: Twente sits on thick salt layers, and this small museum covers every side of salt, from preserving food to Roman pay, plus a collection of more than 2,000 salt shakers.
new.tip: Pair it with a walk to the Twickel estate on the edge of Delden.

new.title: Fire up the steam engines at Oyfo in Hengelo
new.desc: Hengelo grew on the factories of Stork and Hazemeijer, and the Oyfo Techniekmuseum traces 150 years of Twente industry, from steam engines and textiles to radar and space travel.
new.tip: It sits on the old Hazemeijer site, a short walk from the Twentse Bierbrouwerij for a drink afterwards.

new.title: See the sails turn at Pelmolen Ter Horst in Rijssen
new.desc: Built in 1752, this listed oil and barley mill still presses oil when the wind blows, worked by volunteer millers.
new.tip: Come on a breezy day when the millers are in; Rijssen's little narrow gauge railway is another local curiosity.

new.title: Visit a linen merchant's home in Borne
new.desc: The Bussemakerhuis of 1655 is the only surviving manufacturer's house of its kind in Overijssel; the Bussemakers gave yarn to Twente home weavers and sold their linen in Holland.
new.tip: It is a short walk from Borne station on the Hengelo to Almelo line.

new.title: Taste ice cream at Hellendoorn's Bakery and Ice Cream Museum
new.desc: Old dough kneaders, a 1924 steam engine and the first ice lolly machines fill this village museum, which ends in a coffee room serving ice cream and Twente bakes.
new.tip: In school holidays children can help bake a bread roll; combine it with a hike on the nearby Sallandse Heuvelrug.

new.title: Order krentewegge and pancakes at In Den Markenrichter
new.desc: This country pancake house outside Delden serves around 120 kinds of pannenkoeken on a big garden terrace, and real Twentse krentewegge with your coffee.
new.tip: Cycle there from Delden or the Twickel estate; there is a seasonal pancake of the month.
new.q: De Pannenkoekerie In Den Markenrichter Rijksweg 18 Ambt Delden

new.title: Refuel at Pannenkoekhoes De Stroper in De Lutte
new.desc: Tucked into the green around De Lutte, De Stroper serves classic and unusual pancakes, a natural pause between forest walks on the Twente border.
new.tip: Combine it with the Tankenberg or the Lutterzand, both a short ride away.

new.title: Eat pancakes by Watermolen Bels near Mander
new.desc: In the quiet northeast of Twente, close to Vasse, a working watermill on a brook sets the scene for pancakes in a terrace by the water.
new.tip: Cycle there from Ootmarsum or Vasse through the Springendal; the nearby Watermolen van Frans runs nature activities for kids.
